Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Consistent assessment findings: New, persistent, severe headache for ~3 days with photophobia and occasional visual phenomena; no fever or systemic illness; partial relief with NSAIDs; affects daily functioning; planned neurological examination and fundoscopy; consideration of migraine as a leading diagnosis; discussion of potential need to adjust hormonal contraception if migrainous features persist.
- Summary of likely contributing or alternative diagnoses from DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Migraine with aura (migraine-type headache) – High
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) related to estrogen-containing oral contraceptive – Moderate
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension – Medium
  - Intracranial mass / raised intracranial pressure – Low
  - Meningitis/encephalitis – Low
- Note on contradictions: Not observed in transcript; no conflicts identified.

Management Plan
- management_plan_main_or_not_recorded:
  - Schedule full neurological examination with fundoscopy (via appointment with support line)
  - Begin analgesic plan: prescription for a medication similar to ibuprofen to use when needed; to be taken with food; paracetamol may be used concurrently
  - Blood pressure to be checked at subsequent examination to assess suitability of ongoing hormonal therapy
  - Discuss possible adjustment of oral contraceptive pill if migrainous features persist or worsen
  - If headaches worsen, change in pattern, or new neurologic symptoms arise, instruct to seek urgent evaluation (A&E)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Migraine with aura (migraine-type headache)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Photophobia, visual phenomena, new persistent severe headache, partial NSAID relief, family history of migraines
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) related to estrogen-containing oral contraceptive
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: New, persistent headache in a patient on combined OCP; requires imaging to rule out
- Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Female with headaches and visual symptoms; would warrant fundoscopy and consideration of IIH
- Intracranial mass / raised intracranial pressure
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Morning predominance and persistent headache could occur with intracranial mass, but acute 3-day onset without focal signs lowers likelihood
- Meningitis/encephalitis
  - Likelihood: Low
  - Justification: Photophobia present but absence of fever, meningismus, or altered mental status makes infectious/inflammatory etiology less likely
